summary: Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indologist and historian. He earned an MPhil from Vikram University, where he was attested as a research scholar in 2014.
Mohammad Habib (1895–1971) was an Indian historian. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University (~1911–1915), the University of Allahabad (~1915–1916), and New College, Oxford (~1916–1920).

Mokurai Shimaji (1838–1911) was a Japanese scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū. He served at Nishi Hongan-ji (1870), was chief executive at Hongan-ji, and became the 25th head priest at Gankyo-ji in 1892.

Mona Schrempf is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin in 2001 and held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University in 2006.

Monica Esposito (1962–2011) was an Italian scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned her PhD from Paris Diderot University (~1988–1993). She completed postdoctoral studies at Ca' Foscari, the Sorbonne, and Kansai University, and was appointed associate professor at Kyoto University in 2003.

Monier Monier-Williams (1819–1899) was a British Indologist and linguist who studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College (1844–1858) and Cheltenham College (~1856–1860) before serving as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit from 1860.

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach (born 1941) is a German scholar of Indology and linguistics. She completed her doctorate at the Free University of Berlin under Heinz-Jürgen Pinnow and later held professorships at the universities of Bonn, Bamberg, Cologne, and Heidelberg (1990–2006).

Monika Zin (born 1957) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. Educated at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and the University of Munich, she held professorships at Munich (~2000–2015), Berlin (~2015–2016), and Leipzig University (2017).
Moodeen Sheriff (died 1891) was an Indian medical practitioner and Indologist. He studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moriichi Yamazaki (born 1948) is a Japanese scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Tohoku University and Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman, later holding posts at Sendai National College of Technology (1991–2003) and Hosen Gakuen College (2005).

Moritz Abraham Stern (1807–1894) was a German scholar and linguist. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Karl Otfried Müller, subsequently serving as extraordinarius professor at Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

Moriya Okano (born 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Kanto Gakuin University and held appointments at Musashino University and the Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies (~1993).

Moriz Haupt (1808–1874) was a German linguist. He studied at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann, later serving as professor at Leipzig (1841–1851) and Berlin (from 1853), and as perpetual secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1861–1874).

Moriz Winternitz (1863–1937) was an Austrian Indologist. He studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and worked with Friedrich Max Müller, later holding posts at Oxford, Charles University, the German University in Prague (~1902–1934), and Visva-Bharati University (1922–1924).

Morten Schlütter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Copenhagen and Yale under Stanley Weinstein, and held teaching posts at Yale, Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, the University of Wisconsin–Madison, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler (1890–1976) was a British archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London and the University of London. He was director of the National Museum Wales, keeper of the London Museum, and Director-General of Archæology in India (1944–1948).

Morton Klass (1927–2001) was an American anthropologist and Indologist who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, working with Conrad M. Arensberg. He held faculty posts at Bennington College (1959), Barnard College (from 1965), and Columbia University (1982–1985).
Mother Sayamagyi (1925–2017) was a practitioner and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She was a disciple of and the successor to U Ba Khin.

Motohiro Yoritomi (1945–2015) was a Japanese scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his MA and PhD at Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He held professorships at Shuchiin University and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Motoi Ono (born 1958) is a Japanese scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tsukuba under Ekyo Ejima and earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna, later becoming an associate professor at Tsukuba.
